name: Core Stats
content:
Each character has three CORE STATS: BODY, HEART and WITS.

Each core stat has a score between 0 and 15. A character's initial scores are determined when the character is created (see the Character Creation section) and generally increase as a character gains experience (see the Character Advancement section).

Each core stat has five skills that fall under its domain, as well as one virtue, one weakness and one state, shown here in the core section of the Renaissance character sheet:

SKILLS represent a character's aptitudes that are generally useful in the course of adventuring. Any character may use any skill at any time (if the GM deems it appropriate for the situation) but their chances of success are increased as they gain ranks in a given skill, up to a maximum of 5 ranks. Each rank adds one success die (d6) to the dice pool for checks made with that skill. If a character has no ranks in a skill, they only roll a fate die (d12), with no success dice.

Each VIRTUE is a resource derived from its associated core stat. Its base value is determined by that core stat's score, and its current value changes over the course of gameplay.

Each virtue is countered by a WEAKNESS. Weaknesses represent vulnerabilities accumulated over the course of gameplay. Weaknesses only have a current score (no base value) and start at zero by default.

When a weakness outweighs its associated virtue, the character is in a STATE. Each state has two levels of severity: the first applies a -1d (one rank) penalty to all skills in its column, the second applies a general penalty to all skill checks, which varies by state.

Below are detailed descriptions of each core stat's skills, virtue, weakness and state:

BODY

BODY represents a character’s physical capabilities and power.

SKILLS

AWE is used to impress or intimidate others with your appearance or with physical feats:  Strike an impressive posture. Hold a sword to a captive’s neck. List your accomplishments in a booming voice.

STRENGTH is used for physical actions that require sustained effort or brute force:  Swing a cudgel. Scale a high rampart. Flip a heavy cart. Break down a door. Chase a fleeing foe. Swim against the current.

DEXTERITY is used for physical actions that require finesse or a quick reaction:  Aim a bow. Throw a dagger. Pick a lock. Dodge an explosion. Land on your feet. Grab a ledge as you fall.

FORTITUDE is used to withstand physical hardship or discomfort:  Endure cold. Resist poison. Press on through hunger and thirst. Overcome the physical effects of a spell.

CRAFT is used to make or mend things by hand:  Set a trap. Build an improvised raft. Make camp in a defensive position. Mend a torn waterskin. Hammer a circlet into shape. Tie a strong knot.

ENDURANCE

ENDURANCE is a virtue that represents a character’s physical stamina. It is generally reduced by strenuous activity or harm suffered in combat and is restored through rest (see Rest & Recovery).

Your base Endurance is 5 times your BODY score. You start with a current Endurance score equal to your base Endurance.

When a character is reduced to 0 Endurance, they fall unconscious and wake up one hour later with 1 Endurance, unless they are in the Twice Helpless state (see WITS below).

LOAD

LOAD is a weakness that represents the weight and discomfort caused by the clothing, armor, weapons and other equipment you’re carrying.

Your current Load is equal to the weight you are carrying, in pounds, minus your base Endurance, minus your BODY score. For example, a character carrying 20 pounds of gear with a base Endurance of 15 and a BODY score of 3 would have a Load score of 2 (20 - 15 - 3 = 2). The minimum for Load is 0; you can’t have a negative Load score.

Note that Load is measured moment-to-moment, so you can choose to drop a heavy pack or other weighty item to reduce your Load score in a pinch.

WEARY

WEARY is a state that represents when the weight and bulk of a character’s equipment begins to affect their performance.

When your Load is equal to or greater than your current Endurance, you are Weary.

While Weary, you take -1d to all skill checks under BODY: Awe, Strength, Dexterity, Fortitude, Craft.

TWICE WEARY

If your Load equals or exceeds your base Endurance, you are TWICE WEARY: on ALL your skill checks (not just those under BODY), success die results of 3 or less don’t count toward the total result for the roll. This is in addition to the effects of Weary.

HEART

HEART represents a character’s force of personality and spiritual strength.

SKILLS

PERFORM is used to delight, enthrall or deceive others:  Sing a song. Cause a distraction. Pretend you're someone else.

INSIGHT is used to perceive the feelings and motivations of others:  Read the room. See through a lie. Sense an ulterior motive.

COURTESY is used to engage your manners and say the right thing:  Introduce yourself to someone important. Buy a drink for a potential ally. Ask a prying question delicately.

SPIRIT is used to call on your willpower and connection to the supernatural:  Cast a spell. Resist a curse. Overcome fear. Commune with a deity.

AID is used to help, heal, guide or comfort others:  Mend a wound. Offer encouragement to an ally. Treat poison. Remind a leader of their purpose.

HOPE

HOPE is a virtue that represents a character’s reserve of spiritual resilience and positivity. It is generally reduced when a player calls upon that reserve to push themselves and is restored through rest and time away from the adventuring life (see the Rest & Recovery section).

Hope can also be earned through great acts of kindness, selflessness or heroism. The GM holds the power to propose awarding Hope for such an act, subject to the group's approval. Because this involves a moral judgment, pause for an above-the-table discussion and reach group consensus on whether Hope should be awarded—and why.

Your base Hope is 2 times your HEART score. You start with a current Hope score equal to your base Hope.

A hopeful character can keep going when physically stronger heroes have already succumbed to despair. At any time, before making a skill check, a player may choose to spend 1 Hope to gain an additional success die (+1d) on the roll. You can only do this once per skill check. When you spend Hope, describe what your character is drawing on to push themself.

When a character is reduced to 0 Hope, they are spiritually drained and cannot push themselves beyond their limits - you cannot go below 0 Hope to gain an additional success die on a skill check.

SHADOW

SHADOW is a weakness that represents a character’s accumulated sense of fear, dread and despair. It starts at 0 and is generally gained by encountering frightful or evil creatures, figures and places. At the GM’s discretion, you may have the opportunity to make a skill check to resist gaining Shadow—most commonly Spirit.

Shadow can also be earned through acts of cruelty, deception, or cowardice. The GM holds the power to propose awarding Shadow for such an act, subject to the group's approval. Because this involves a moral judgment, pause for an above-the-table discussion and reach group consensus on whether Shadow should be awarded—and why.

Shadow is generally reduced by spending time mending spiritual hurt, overcoming fears, or visiting a place of spiritual power or personal significance (see the Rest & Recovery section).

MISERABLE

MISERABLE is a state that represents a character’s shaken will or lost determination.

When your Shadow is equal to or greater than your current Hope, you are Miserable.

While Miserable, you take -1d to all skill checks under HEART: Perform, Insight, Courtesy, Spirit, Aid.

TWICE MISERABLE

If your Shadow equals or exceeds your base Hope, you are TWICE MISERABLE: on ALL your skill checks (not just those under HEART), rolling Morte 💀 on a fate die means the Check automatically fails, regardless of the total. This is in addition to the effects of Miserable.

WITS

WITS represents a character’s intellect and cleverness.

SKILLS

PERSUADE is used to change the minds of others through rhetoric or compromise:  Convince someone that your interests are aligned. Make an offer to recruit a potential ally. Calm an angry mob by explaining yourself.

AWARENESS is used to perceive your surroundings through your senses:  Spy a hidden detail. Hear a conversation through a door. Smell faint smoke. Find a crack in a wall.

STEALTH is used to avoid detection or act discreetly:  Sneak past the guards. Pick a pocket. Hide in a tree. Blend into a crowd. Leave no trace as you travel.

LORE is used to recall knowledge and experience:  Remember details about a town you once visited. Recite a spell from memory. Identify an edible mushroom.

RIDDLE is used for deduction and reasoning:  Suss out the connections between seemingly unrelated clues. Decipher a cryptic poem. Analyze a foe's strategy.

DEFENSE

DEFENSE is a virtue that represents a character’s ability to dodge attacks through skill or cunning. It is generally reduced by penalties imposed by opponents and increased by armor and various abilities and effects.

Your base Defense is equal to your WITS score. You start with a current Defense score equal to your base Defense.

When a character is reduced to 0 Defense, they offer no resistance to physical attacks.

INJURY

INJURY is a weakness that represents the wounds a character has sustained and is currently suffering from.

Injury starts at 0 and generally increases through combat and other adventuring mishaps. It impedes a character's ability to regain Endurance and is the main mechanism by which a character can die. It is generally reduced by lengthy rest and skilled healing. See the Combat and Rest & Recovery sections.

HELPLESS

HELPLESS is a state that represents when a character’s wounds leave them at the mercy of their foes.

When your Injury is equal to or greater than your current Defense, you are Helpless.

While Helpless, you take -1d to all WITS skill checks, and you cannot resist Injury (see the Combat section).

Additionally, being Helpless reduces the amount of Endurance you regain from resting (see the Rest & Recovery section).

TWICE HELPLESS

If your Injury equals or exceeds your base Defense, you are TWICE HELPLESS:  In addition to the effects of Helpless, attacks against your Defense automatically pass, regardless of the attack roll's result, and if your Endurance is or becomes 0, you are dying (see the Combat section).
